name: Mokins Bay Campground
note: Idaho Panhandle NF (Coeur d'Alene River RD) campground set back in forest near the east shore of Hayden Lake (Mokins Bay); the lake is about a 10-minute walk from the loop. Single 14-site loop, RVs/trailers to 50 ft, paved spurs, drinking water, vault toilets, no hookups/dump/showers. Winding paved access road but suitable for larger rigs. Both first-come, first-served and reservable sites (reservable online). --Claude

name: Big Hank Campground
note: Idaho Panhandle NF (Coeur d'Alene River area), on the North Fork Coeur d'Alene River off FH208 ~17 mi N of Prichard. ~30 drive-in sites with paved parking spurs, RVs to 45 ft; vault toilets, hand-pump drinking water, no hookups. Reservable online (unreserved sites go FCFS). --Claude

name: Riley Creek Campground
note: USACE Albeni Falls Project (Riley Creek Recreation Area), the largest rec area, on the Pend Oreille River at Laclede. 67 sites all with electric+water hookups (50/30/20 amp), paved roads, dump station, hot showers, boat ramp, swim beach, playground; RVs to ~44 ft (no pull-throughs, drive-in tight for big rigs). Reservation only (no FCFS), reservable online. --Claude

name: Priest River Recreation Area (The Mudhole)
note: USACE Albeni Falls Project, 'The Mudhole,' at the mouth of the Priest River on the Pend Oreille River, ~1 mi E of Priest River off Hwy 2. 20 drive-in sites, no hookups but on-site RV dump station; flush toilets, hot showers, boat ramp, swim beach, playground; loop paved in 2024. Reservation only (no FCFS), reservable online. --Claude

name: Osprey Campground
note: USFS (Idaho Panhandle NF, Priest Lake RD) campground on the west shore near the south end of Priest Lake. 15 drive-in sites (10 reservable, 5 FCFS) fitting RVs/trailers ~20-64 ft; vault toilets. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Reeder Bay Campground
note: USFS (Idaho Panhandle NF, Priest Lake RD) campground on the west shore of Priest Lake. 24 sites (some FCFS, rest reservable), paved roads/spurs fitting RVs/trailers ~19-55 ft, flush toilets, pressurized water, sandy beach sloping to the lake. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Lud Drexler Park
note: BLM developed park on the east side of Salmon Falls Creek Reservoir, ~7 mi west of Rogerson near Salmon Dam. ~20 developed sites with shade cabanas, fire rings, tables and vault toilets; potable water, RV dump and boat ramp; dispersed sites also. First-come, first-served ($5 day-use). --Claude

name: Balanced Rock Park
note: Twin Falls County park in Salmon Falls Creek canyon south of Buhl, at the creek crossing below the Balanced Rock formation. ~12 informal primitive drive-in sites along the creek; pit toilets, potable water spigots, fire rings/grills and a rentable pavilion; no hookups. First-come, first-served, 7-day limit. --Claude

name: Blackfoot Reservoir Campground
note: BLM campground (Pocatello Field Office) on the southwest shore of Blackfoot Reservoir near Soda Springs; RV Life mis-tagged as DNR. 28 campsites: 16 fully developed with 50-amp electric + potable water and 12 standard; 2 boat ramps, RV dump station. Mostly first-come, first-served (5 sites #10,11,13,14,16 reservable on recreation.gov). Drive-in RV accessible. --Claude

name: Bruneau Dunes State Park
note: IDPR state park at North America's tallest single-structure sand dune, with two small park lakes. Broken Wheel campground (48 sites, 32 with power + water, RVs to ~50 ft) and Eagle Cove campground (50 large sites, 30/50-amp electric + water, big-rig capable) are reservable; additional standard sites and a 19-site FCFS equestrian loop. Drive-in RV accessible. --Claude

name: Cove Recreation Area (CJ Strike Reservoir)
note: BLM Cove Recreation Site (Four Rivers Field Office) on CJ Strike Reservoir, ~8 mi NW of Bruneau; RV Life mis-tagged as DNR. 41 campsites (34 with cabana shade shelters over concrete pads) on packed-gravel/natural loops, no hookups, potable water, RV dump station, fishing docks, boat ramp. First-come, first-served, 14-day limit. Drive-in RV accessible. --Claude

name: Silver City Campground
note: BLM campground in the historic Silver City mining town, Owyhee Mtns ~23 mi of gravel road S of Murphy. 6 sites, first-come, first-served; no potable water (Jordan Creek is mercury-contaminated from old mining — bring water), vault toilets. The Murphy/Hwy-78 approach is well-packed gravel and a 24-ft C-class rig (towing a trailer) has driven in per a firsthand report; high-clearance advised, seasonal (Memorial Day to first snow). --Claude

name: Magic Reservoir
note: BLM-managed semi-developed/dispersed camping around Magic Reservoir (sites incl. Lava Creek, Lava Cove, West Magic, Magic Dam, Myrtle Point); this area is shoreline pull-offs near the dam. Vault toilets, no drinking water, gravel/dirt drive-in access, no hookups. First-come, first-served (new $10/day boat-ramp fee at Magic/Moonstone/West Magic ramps). --Claude

name: Moonstone Access (Magic Reservoir)
note: BLM access site on the north shore of Magic Reservoir with a boat ramp/dock. One developed campsite (metal table, fire ring w/ grill, gravel drive) plus 3-4 primitive sites (stone rings, dirt drives); vault toilet, no water, no hookups. First-come, first-served (new $10/day boat-ramp fee). --Claude

name: Kelly Island Campground
note: BLM campground in a cottonwood gallery forest on the South Fork Snake River, ~23 mi NE of Idaho Falls (gravel access road off Kelly Canyon rd). 14 single sites ($10) + doubles, pull-throughs, central water spigot, vault toilets, day-use area, boat access; no hookups; pets not permitted; seasonal gate (May-Sep). Singles FCFS; 1 group site (fits ~4 large RVs) reservable online. --Claude

name: Joe T. Fallini Recreation Site
note: BLM campground on Mackay Reservoir, ~6 mi N of Mackay on US-93, with views of the Lost River Range. 26 sites in two loops: Grouse (14 single RV sites w/ power+water hookups, 4 tent sites) and Chukar (4 double + 4 single RV sites w/ power+water); dump station, restrooms, drinking water, boat ramp. First-come, first-served (scan-and-pay via rec.gov app). --Claude

name: McCrea Bridge Campground
note: Caribou-Targhee NF (Ashton/Island Park RD) on the backwaters of Island Park Reservoir at the McCrea Bridge over Henrys Fork. 19 single + 4 double sites, no hookups, vault toilets, drinking water, boat ramp in the campground; RVs to 65 ft. Reservable online in season (FCFS after hours). Reservoir draws down for irrigation and by August water recedes from the campground. --Claude

name: Horsethief Reservoir Campground
note: Valley County Parks & Recreation (managed since 2026 in partnership with Idaho Fish & Game), ~9 mi E of Cascade on 260-acre Horsethief Reservoir (no-wake, 5 mph). Primitive; several loops (King's Landing, Bear Knob, Easters Cove, Timber Bay, Osprey) on the N/NW shore, vault toilets, potable water, fire pits, no hookups. Suitable for rigs 30 ft and under. Cash or check, first-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Spring Gulch Campground
note: BLM Challis Field Office campground on the Upper Salmon River, ~10 mi north of Challis on US-93. 10 drive-in sites, potable water, vault toilets, river/fishing access; no hookups. First-come, first-served, open May-Oct. --Claude

name: Cottonwood Recreation Site (BLM)
note: BLM Challis Field Office site on the Upper Salmon River, ~14 mi N of Challis on US-93. 13 FCFS drive-in campsites (+2 walk-in tent), potable water, vault toilets, dump station, boat ramp; no hookups. First-come, first-served (group pavilion reservable). --Claude

name: Smokey Cubs Recreation Site (BLM)
note: BLM Salmon Field Office campground ~4 mi NE of Leadore off SH-29 toward Bannock Pass, at the base of the Beaverhead Mtns. 8 sites suited to RVs/trailers and tents, water, vault toilets; first-come, first-served, open May-Oct. --Claude

name: Morgan Bar Recreation Site
note: BLM Salmon Field Office campground ~7 mi north of Salmon on the west bank of the Salmon River (via Diamond Creek Rd). Medium-sized campground, ~8 RV/tent sites, potable water, vault toilets, boat ramp, group picnic area; no hookups. First-come, first-served (rec.gov Scan & Pay). Camp host Memorial Day-Labor Day. --Claude

name: Tower Rock Recreation Site
note: BLM Salmon Field Office campground ~10 mi north of Salmon between Hwy 93 and the Salmon River; a Lewis & Clark overnight site. 4 standard nonelectric RV sites plus 2 tent-only, no hookups, vault toilets, picnic shelter, fishing platforms, boat ramp. First-come, first-served (rec.gov Scan & Pay). --Claude

name: Hammer Creek Recreation Site
note: BLM Cottonwood Field Office campground on the Lower Salmon River, ~2.7 mi off Hwy 95 west of White Bird; popular boater put-in. 12 RV/tent sites, drinking water, flush & vault toilets, RV dump station, changing rooms, boat ramp; no hookups. First-come, first-served ($10/night). --Claude

name: Pine Bar Recreation Site
note: BLM Cottonwood Field Office site on the Lower Salmon River, ~11 mi south of Cottonwood via (mostly paved) Graves Creek Rd; boater put-in with sandy beaches. 6 designated numbered sites with loop pull-arounds; small campground best for moderate-size rigs, scout ahead. First-come, first-served ($7/night). --Claude

name: Pink House Recreation Site
note: BLM Cottonwood Field Office campground on the Clearwater River ~5 mi west of Orofino. 15 full-hookup RV sites (water/30-amp/sewer, RVs to 40 ft; 2 pull-through, rest back-in) plus 3 tent sites, flush & vault toilets, potable water, boat ramp, full-time camp host. First-come, first-served (rec.gov Scan & Pay, not reservable in advance). --Claude

name: Round Lake State Park
note: Small Idaho State Park on 58-acre Round Lake near Sagle. Campground has 51 sites: 16 serviced back-in sites with 30-amp electric + water (max RV ~24 ft), plus standard sites; flush toilets, showers, dump station. Reservable ~mid-May to early Sept, FCFS the rest of the year. Small back-in sites — a 23-ft rig fits, no big rigs. --Claude

Fees: non-residents pay double the base rate, add-ons the same

name: Twin Falls County Fairgrounds RV Park
note: Twin Falls County Fairgrounds RV area on the east side of the grounds, Filer. ~80 full-hookup (water/sewer/50-amp) plus ~100 water/30-amp sites; grass sites, dirt roads, individual enclosed shower/toilet units. First-come, first-served, cash/check; call after-hours number to be sited. Camps year-round outside fair week (verify around fairground events). --Claude

name: Ricketts RV Camp
note: Primitive RV camp at Snake River Canyons Park off Shoshone Falls Rd north of Twin Falls. BLM land leased to Jerome County and run by the local Snake River Canyons Park board. 13 level paved RV pads (pull-in/pull-through) with picnic table + fire ring, 2 vault toilets, no hookups; separate equestrian/overflow area (general campground, not horse-only). First-come, first-served, 5-night limit. --Claude

name: Jerome County Fairgrounds
note: Jerome County fairgrounds; non-fair RV camping on paved pull-through lots with 30-amp electric + water, ~$20/night, roughly mid-April to mid-Oct; no on-site restrooms (store/gas a block away). Self-pay at the office, no reservations; spaces limited during fair/events. --Claude

name: Big Wood River RV Park
note: Gooding County-run RV park ~1 mi north of Gooding along ID-46 by the Big Wood River; 25 sites (~20 RV) with water + 30/50-amp electric, showers and flush toilets, plus tent sites; open year-round, first-come first-served, no reservations. --Claude

name: Old Fort Boise RV Park
note: City of Parma park at the Old Fort Boise replica. 8 first-come, first-served gravel sites with electric and water hookups, sewer dump ($10), showers ($5), restrooms, playground; grassy park, RVs up to ~50 ft, 7-day limit in 30 days, tents not allowed on the grass; some industrial noise from a nearby factory. --Claude

name: Beaver Dick Park
note: Madison County park on the west bank of Henry's Fork of the Snake River, ~4.5 mi west of Rexburg. Mixed tent/RV dry camping (no hookups, no potable water), vault toilets, picnic tables, fire rings, playground, boat ramp, disc golf; adjacent BLM land. First-come, first-served, 5-night max in 30 days. --Claude

name: Emmett RV Park (City)
note: City of Emmett municipal RV park at 400 E 12th St by the Gem County fairgrounds. Full hookups (water/sewer, 30/50-amp), 60-ft-deep pull-in stalls, coin showers, dump station ($3), WiFi; year-round, first-come first-served, 10-day max; campers must be model-year 2000+, no tents. --Claude

name: Robinson County Park
note: Latah County park ~5 mi east of Moscow on Robinson Lake, 54 acres. 5 RV sites with 20/30/50-amp hookups ($25), plus primitive tent sites ($15); vault toilets/porta-potties, no showers. First-come, first-served, 14-day limit per 28-day period. Access is via neighborhood roads with some low power lines - tall rigs (over 13 ft) use caution; 23-ft length is fine. --Claude

name: Spring Valley Reservoir Campground
note: Latah County park on 49-acre Spring Valley Reservoir, ~3 mi north of Troy. RV area has 10 pull-through sites with power and water; primitive tent camping $15. Picnic shelter, swim beach, boat ramp (electric motors only), fish-cleaning station. First-come, first-served, 14-day limit per 28-day period; county took over camping management. --Claude

name: Fairway RV Park
note: Seasonal (Apr-mid-Oct) RV park operated by the Eastern Idaho State Fair in Blackfoot; 45+ water/electric drive-in sites incl large pull-thrus, dump station, restrooms/showers. First-come, first-served — honor-system lockbox pay (no reservations); recent ~$30/night. Sites fit ~30 ft; larger rigs buy two. Open all season, not event-only. --Claude

name: Juniper Campground (Ririe Reservoir)
note: Bonneville County-run campground on Ririe Reservoir. Multiple loops (A/B reservable online, C first-come, first-served); mix of full-hookup, dry-dock, and tent sites; boat launch, fishing docks, vault restrooms. --Claude

name: Egin Lakes Campground
note: BLM campground in the St. Anthony Sand Dunes SRMA, ~8 mi west of St. Anthony; 48 improved drive-in units with electric pedestals (50/30/120v), potable water hydrants, RV dump station, fire rings, vault toilets; 26 sites reservable online and 22 first-come, first-served; popular OHV/sand-dune area. --Claude

name: Stanley Lake Campground
note: Sawtooth National Forest / Sawtooth NRA campground on a hillside above Stanley Lake, in lodgepole pine at ~6,500 ft. About 39 sites across three loops (Lakeview Loop 1-6, main loop 7-24, Loop 2 25-39); no hookups, vault toilets, drinking water. 17 sites reservable, remainder first-come, first-served. Boat ramp just outside the campground. --Claude
